speaker: Avery Santana
cascadeSummary: I am requiring verifiable records before final action on the West Oakland charter renewal, alternative-response expansion, Grand Lake and tenant defense. Fruitvale design and Baylight milestone certification remain evidence-held; the youth apprenticeship program is recorded as stalled until its overdue placement-gap analysis and adjustment plan are published. INIT-014's filing claim is corrected to unverified, INIT-015 remains announced after a missed filing deadline, and the petition ledger needs a Clerk-backed crosswalk. The city will also follow up on the Glenview and Piedmont Avenue spikes while making room for civic life.

statements.topic: West Oakland Stabilization Fund charter renewal
statements.decision: Keep the transmitted charter renewal ordinance on this cycle's Council calendar; require verified C114 closeout publication before final action, with business-and-resident scope and the 23-day standard intact.
statements.quote: West Oakland's renewal must bring its closeout ledger, its business-and-resident charter and its 23-day standard into the same public record.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland should consider the $28 million West Oakland Stabilization Fund charter renewal this cycle, with the business-and-resident scope and 23-day processing standard intact. I agree with Deputy Mayor Okoro and Councilmember Crane: the C114 closeout publication must be in the hearing record and verified before a final renewal decision. I am keeping the transmitted ordinance on the Council calendar on those conditions, not declaring renewal approved. The Fund's existing disbursement work continues under its charter. Council should see the closeout ledger and the exact renewal language before it acts; public money deserves a public record.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C116: Charter renewal kept on Council calendar; final action requires verified C114 closeout, business-and-resident scope and the 23-day standard.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Verify C114 closeout and conduct Council charter-renewal consideration

statements.topic: D3 Fruitvale alternative-response briefing and expansion hold
statements.decision: Direct execution and publication of the D3 Fruitvale briefing record with district-level and Fruitvale data; hold expansion pending that record, the D5 audit and the Baylight feasibility review.
statements.quote: Before alternative response grows, Fruitvale should be able to read the data, attend the briefing and inspect the unfinished work.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland's alternative response work should be judged by what residents can inspect, not by how quickly we can announce another district. I agree with Councilmembers Delgado and Rivers. I am directing execution and publication of the D3 Fruitvale briefing record this cycle, including district-level and Fruitvale data and documented community participation. The record must also name responsible offices and next dates for the incomplete D5 audit and Baylight feasibility review. Expansion remains held until that work is complete. This $12.5 million initiative continues its existing dispatch work; nothing in this decision authorizes a new district or declares the evaluation finished.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C116: D3 Fruitvale briefing execution and publication directed; expansion held pending community documentation, D5 audit and Baylight feasibility review.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Execute and publish D3 Fruitvale briefing record; file D5 and Baylight next dates

statements.topic: Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II design evidence
statements.initiative: Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II — Visioning
statements.decision: Hold further design advancement until preliminary schematics are delivered and a documented Fruitvale public comment-and-response record is published; preserve the C86 authorization.
statements.quote: Phase II stays authorized, but the next design step must be earned with schematics and a real Fruitvale response record.
statements.fullStatement: Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II remains a $230 million commitment authorized by Council at C86, and I am not walking away from it. I am holding further design advancement until the preliminary schematics are delivered and Fruitvale residents have a documented public comment-and-response record. The packet does not include either completed deliverable, and the low-severity improvement flag is not a substitute for that evidence. The next milestone must show what was presented, how the community responded, what changed and what remains unresolved. That is how we protect the binding visioning framework while keeping this project moving honestly.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C116: Further design advancement held pending preliminary schematics and a documented Fruitvale public comment-and-response record.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Deliver schematics and publish Fruitvale comment-and-response record

statements.decision: Require the Q3 clinical intake audit filing with HCAI and the Council Clerk and completion of the Telegraph and 47th merchant walkthrough before certifying operational oversight.
statements.quote: Temescal's open doors deserve open books: file the Q3 audit, walk the merchant corridor, then certify oversight.
statements.fullStatement: The Temescal Community Health Center is open, and our job now is to keep its operations accountable. Councilmember Ashford's oversight condition is reasonable. I am requiring the Q3 clinical intake audit to be filed with HCAI and the Council Clerk and the recurring merchant verification walkthrough at Telegraph and 47th to be completed on schedule. I will not certify operational oversight from the calendar alone; both records must be verifiable. The center's $45 million public investment already has a standing utilization-audit practice. This cycle should continue that discipline without inventing a new problem or claiming a result before the filings arrive.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C116: Q3 intake audit filing and Telegraph & 47th merchant walkthrough required before operational oversight is certified.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: File Q3 audit with HCAI and Clerk; complete merchant walkthrough

statements.topic: Baylight construction milestone and continuing oversight
statements.decision: Decline to certify a construction milestone; require the evidence-file review while independent remediation verification, hotline, dust-control and workforce oversight continue.
statements.quote: I will measure Baylight by verified remediation and workforce records, not by upbeat streets or an approaching calendar date.
statements.fullStatement: Baylight's $2.1 billion project continues with independent remediation oversight, the construction hotline, dust control on haul routes and Jack London workforce coordination. I am not declaring a construction milestone passed. The C115 evidence file must be reviewed against the actual milestone standard, with independent remediation verification and the hotline, dust-control and workforce records included. Low-severity improvement flags in Jack London and Downtown are welcome, but they are not engineering evidence. My decision is to keep construction-active oversight in place and require the evidence-file review before any milestone certification. Oakland can celebrate progress without confusing it with completion.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C116: No construction milestone certified; evidence-file review and independent remediation, hotline, dust-control and workforce oversight continue.

statements.decision: Record INIT-007 as stalled pending publication of the placement-gap analysis and adjustment plan, with explicit West Oakland and Fruitvale review and no further phase advancement.
statements.quote: Four cycles without the required placement record means we record the stall, publish the gaps, and fix who the program reaches.
statements.fullStatement: Four cycles without movement require an honest status, not another announcement of momentum. The packet does not include the required placement-gap analysis and adjustment plan, and I will not manufacture their publication. I am recording INIT-007 as stalled until those documents are published and verified. The analysis must explicitly review West Oakland and Fruitvale, evaluate who placements are reaching, identify specific program adjustments and name responsibility for the next report. The $12.5 million budget does not excuse a missing deliverable. This is accountability for a program Oakland needs, not a claim that its mission has ended.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C116: Recorded stalled pending publication of the placement-gap analysis and adjustment plan, including West Oakland and Fruitvale review.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Publish placement-gap analysis and program adjustment plan

statements.decision: Keep INIT-009 vote-scheduled, support YES with every Chen-Vega condition intact, and require a Clerk-certified full-council roll call before claiming any outcome or appropriation.
statements.quote: My YES on Grand Lake comes with every safeguard attached, and it still requires a Clerk-certified council roll call.
statements.fullStatement: I remain a YES on Commercial Stabilization for Grand Lake because the $2.5 million proposal now carries milestone reporting and audit protocols. Councilmember Chen's hearing statement records her own YES, but one member's position is not council enactment. I am keeping INIT-009 at vote-scheduled and asking Council to complete the recorded vote this cycle and the City Clerk to certify it with every Chen-Vega condition intact. Until that certified record exists, I will claim neither passage nor defeat, and no appropriation should be inferred. Grand Lake deserves a decision that can be verified, not another cycle of statements mistaken for action.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C116: Full-council decision remains vote-scheduled; certified Clerk roll call required with all Chen-Vega conditions and no outcome claimed.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Hold and certify full-council roll call with Chen-Vega conditions

statements.topic: West Oakland tenant-defense analysis and committee record
statements.decision: Require publication of the legal-support analysis before the committee vote, followed by a Clerk-recorded committee decision; claim no approval, rejection or funding now.
statements.quote: No tenant-defense vote should outrun its legal analysis, and no decision should be announced before the committee record exists.
statements.fullStatement: The $4.2 million West Oakland Tenant Defense Fund proposal needs a public legal-support analysis before the Housing and Community Development Committee records its decision. I am directing that sequence: publish the analysis, hold the committee vote and file the result with the Clerk. The packet supplies neither the analysis nor a committee outcome, so I am not claiming approval, rejection or funding today. This is not a reason to let the proposal disappear. It is a reason to make the next record complete, with the responsible committee, the proposed remedy and the next procedural date visible to residents.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C116: Legal-support analysis must precede the committee vote; no decision or funding outcome claimed pending a Clerk-recorded result.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Publish legal-support analysis and record committee decision

statements.topic: INIT-014 filing correction and Ivy Hill review hold
statements.decision: Correct the C115 filing claim to unverified, keep INIT-014 announced and hold Council review until the Clerk supplies a docket reference or records that filing did not occur.
statements.quote: The honest status of INIT-014 is unverified filing; Ivy Hill deserves facts and a docket reference, not procedural spin.
statements.fullStatement: My C115 closing statement said INIT-014 was filed, but this packet supplies no Clerk reference and the live tracker still shows announced. I am correcting the public account: filing is unverified, and I cannot assert that it occurred. Councilmember Vega's condition is the right one. Council review of the Ivy Hill Community Support Initiative is held until the Clerk supplies a verifiable docket reference or records that the deadline was missed. If no reference exists, the record must say not filed. The underlying evidence remains limited and clear: Ivy Hill has low crime, slow trade and a soured mood. The $2.5 million proposal should be reviewed on those facts, without a manufactured emergency.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C116: C115 filing claim is unverified; Council review held pending a Clerk docket reference or a recorded missed deadline.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Supply Clerk filing reference or record missed deadline

statements.decision: Record the legislation-filing deadline as missed, keep INIT-015 announced, and require a defined cleanup scope, direct outreach and Clerk-verified filing before advancement.
statements.quote: Laurel's cleanup proposal stays announced today; the way forward is a finished scope, real outreach and Clerk-verified legislation.
statements.fullStatement: Laurel needs a defined cleanup scope, direct outreach and visible follow-through, not an unverified filing claim. INIT-015 remains announced, and the legislation-filing step due this cycle has not been verified. I am recording that missed deadline and keeping the $6 million proposal in announced status while the drafting and outreach are completed. The next submission must go to the Clerk with a reference that residents and Council can check. I agree with Councilmember Mobley that a missed verification should be recorded honestly; the remedy is to finish the work and file it properly, not to relabel the calendar.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C116: Legislation-filing deadline missed; INIT-015 remains announced pending scope, outreach and Clerk-verified filing.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Complete scope and outreach; obtain Clerk-verified filing

statements.topic: Petition-response docket reconciliation and INIT-008 record correction
statements.decision: Request the Clerk's docket record and direct a complaint-by-complaint crosswalk; withdraw any implication of ledger completion and decline to confirm an INIT-008 vote or Chinatown or Uptown appropriations.
statements.quote: Seven statements do not resolve ten complaints; Oakland needs the docket-by-docket record, responsible offices, remedies and next dates.
statements.fullStatement: Planning Director Mara Vance is right to demand a reconciliation. This packet contains neither the ten-complaint ledger nor the seven response docket references, so I will not invent a crosswalk. I am asking the City Clerk to supply the docket record and directing my office to publish a complaint-by-complaint crosswalk showing which complaints the seven responses cover, every remaining complaint's status, responsible office, proposed remedy and next date, tied to promises P-d94459ae1189b667 and P-b87ef751a66c370d. Until then, any implication that the ledger is complete is withdrawn. Councilmember Tran is also right to seek the Clerk's record: I cannot confirm an INIT-008 legislative vote or Chinatown or Uptown appropriations, and my office will not assert them.

statements.topic: Glenview and Piedmont Avenue spikes, neighborhood conditions and civic life
statements.decision: Require factual status updates and service next steps for the two medium-severity spikes, maintain attention to neighborhoods with slow or struggling trade, and support this cycle's civic events without declaring a broader emergency.
statements.quote: Reliable services in Glenview and Piedmont Avenue and room for neighborhood joy are not competing priorities; Oakland needs both.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland's economy is stable and crime is low across the neighborhoods listed this cycle, but a medium-severity public-works spike in Glenview and a medium-severity health spike on Piedmont Avenue still require accountable follow-up. I want the responsible teams to publish what is known, the service response and the next update without exaggerating either event. I am also listening to Ivy Hill's soured mood, San Antonio's struggling trade and the slower conditions in Dimond, Glenview, Laurel and Baylight. And yes, Oakland can do that work while making room for the Kelley, Horn and Keane family block parties. Reliable services, economic opportunity and civic joy belong in the same city.
